course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
unit.description: Compare additive and multiplicative change, then build, compose, invert, and model with exponential and logarithmic functions, including residuals and semi-log plots.

quiz.title: Unit 2 FRQ 3: Symbolic manipulations (Topics 2.9 to 2.15)
quiz.headline: Rewrite logarithmic and exponential expressions, solve exponential and logarithmic equations exactly, and find an inverse.
quiz.promptTitle: Free response 3 · Symbolic manipulations · no calculator
quiz.prompt: This question has three parts that each give different functions. Work each part without a calculator.
quiz.instructions: Part B style: no calculator is allowed. Unless otherwise specified, the domain of a function f is the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number. Solutions to equations must be real numbers. Determine the exact value of any expression that can be obtained without a calculator, such as log₂ 8. Unless otherwise specified, combine terms using algebraic methods and rules for exponents and logarithms. Show the work that leads to your answers.
quiz.note: Original practice question written in the AP Precalculus free-response format (6 points, parts A to C). Scoring is self-assessed with the point-by-point rubric. It is not an official AP question or an official AP score.

items: Part A: g(x) = 2 log₃ x − log₃ (9x) and h(x) = 4^(x + 1)·2^(−x).
Part B: j(x) = e^(2x) − 5eˣ + 6 and k(x) = log₂ (x + 2) + log₂ (x − 1).

scaffold.label: Show work
scaffold.text: Write the setup, such as the expression you evaluate or the equation you solve, before the answer.

scaffold.label: Use notation
scaffold.text: Use limit notation, interval notation, and units exactly where a part asks for them.

scaffold.label: Justify
scaffold.text: When a part says give a reason or explain, refer to the given values or the context.

responseFields.label: Part A (i)
responseFields.prompt: A (i). Rewrite g(x) as a single logarithm base 3 without negative exponents in any part of the expression. Your result should be of the form log₃ (expression).
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part A (ii)
responseFields.prompt: A (ii). Rewrite h(x) in the form a·bˣ, where a and b are constants.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (i)
responseFields.prompt: B (i). Solve j(x) = 0 for values of x in the domain of j.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (ii)
responseFields.prompt: B (ii). Solve k(x) = 2 for values of x in the domain of k.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (i)
responseFields.prompt: C (i). Find an expression for m⁻¹(x), the inverse function of m.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (ii)
responseFields.prompt: C (ii). What is the domain of m⁻¹? Give a reason for your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

review.label: Domain and range of an inverse

rubric.label: A (i) Single logarithm
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for g(x) = log₃ (x/9), for x > 0, with work such as log₃ x² − log₃ (9x) = log₃ (x²/(9x)).

rubric.label: A (ii) Form a·bˣ
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for h(x) = 4·2ˣ, with work such as 4^(x + 1) = 4·4ˣ = 4·2^(2x), then 4·2^(2x)·2^(−x) = 4·2ˣ.

rubric.label: B (i) Solutions of j(x) = 0
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for x = ln 2 and x = ln 3, from (eˣ − 2)(eˣ − 3) = 0.

rubric.label: B (ii) Solution of k(x) = 2
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for x = 2 only, with x = −3 rejected because it is not in the domain of k.

rubric.label: C (i) Inverse expression
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for m⁻¹(x) = log₅ ((x − 1)/3) + 2, or an equivalent expression.

rubric.label: C (ii) Domain with reason
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for x > 1, with the reason that the range of m is y > 1 (because 3(5)^(x − 2) > 0), and the domain of m⁻¹ is the range of m.

quiz.modelResponse:
A (i). g(x) = 2 log₃ x − log₃ (9x) = log₃ x² − log₃ (9x) = log₃ (x²/(9x)) = log₃ (x/9), for x > 0.

A (ii). h(x) = 4^(x + 1)·2^(−x) = 4·4ˣ·2^(−x) = 4·(2²)ˣ·2^(−x) = 4·2^(2x)·2^(−x) = 4·2ˣ.

B (i). Let u = eˣ. Then u² − 5u + 6 = 0, so (u − 2)(u − 3) = 0. eˣ = 2 or eˣ = 3, so x = ln 2 or x = ln 3.

B (ii). log₂ ((x + 2)(x − 1)) = 2, so (x + 2)(x − 1) = 4. Then x² + x − 2 = 4, x² + x − 6 = 0, and (x + 3)(x − 2) = 0. x = −3 is not in the domain of k because x − 1 = −4 < 0. So x = 2.

C (i). y = 3(5)^(x − 2) + 1. Reverse x and y: x = 3(5)^(y − 2) + 1. Then (x − 1)/3 = 5^(y − 2), so y − 2 = log₅ ((x − 1)/3) and m⁻¹(x) = log₅ ((x − 1)/3) + 2.

C (ii). Because 3(5)^(x − 2) > 0 for every x, the range of m is y > 1. The domain of m⁻¹ is the range of m, so the domain of m⁻¹ is x > 1. This also matches the requirement (x − 1)/3 > 0 for the logarithm.
quiz.alternateModel: In A (i) you may first write 2 log₃ x − (log₃ 9 + log₃ x) = log₃ x − 2 and then rewrite −2 as −log₃ 9 to get log₃ (x/9). In C (i), m⁻¹(x) = log₅ (x − 1) − log₅ 3 + 2 is an equivalent expression.
commonErrors: Writing log₃ (2x − 9x) by combining coefficients inside the logarithm.
Writing 4^(x + 1)·2^(−x) = 8^(1) or another product of bases.
Taking ln of each term of e^(2x) − 5eˣ + 6 separately.
Subtracting 2 instead of adding 2 when undoing the exponent x − 2.
